summary.intent: Plan and execute GSD Phase 69 (port CipherBox's node/v3 model to the Rust FUSE/WinFsp desktop stack, adding grant-root awareness), then, per user pushback, wire real desktop root-key recovery so a desktop-e2e run can genuinely validate the migration before the phase is called complete.
summary.outcome: Phase 69 planning and execution progressed through repeated re-scoping (14→25 plans) as three successive architectural gaps were discovered mid-execution; the atomic FUSE node/v3 cutover was eventually landed via an 11-slice grind, 19/20 non-Windows plans merged workspace-green, and a follow-on 5-plan root-key-recovery port (69-21..25) was authored and executed through 69-24 (bridge deleted, real keys wired to mount) by the end of the transcript, with 69-25 and the actual desktop-e2e completion run still pending.

repo: D-04 'clean flag-day cutover' forbids any legacy↔node/v3 adapter (no From<FolderMetadata> for Node, etc.) — migrations must fully replace, not bridge.
D-07 dual-keying: read plane keyed by ipnsName (SealedChildRef), write plane keyed by childId UUID (WriteChildRef) — must never be conflated; verified in tests as child_id != ipns_name.
Terminal-owner zeroization is enforced by the type system: parent_read_key/write_key are passed as borrows (&[u8]), so the compiler prevents zeroing caller-owned buffers.

The Rust FUSE mount is a read-WRITE vault owner (it signs IPNS records and seals new children), unlike the TS web 68.2 mirror which is read-only — so read-only listing infra (list_folder) was insufficient and a write-owner materialization API (list_folder_owned) had to be built from scratch.

SC#6 (single gated read entrypoint) is enforced via a CI grep gate for raw resolve_ipns_verified/resolve_published_node calls, with `// sc6-allow:` markers for allowlisted legacy sites (recycle-bin, vault reencrypt).
The desktop's node/v3 root keys were only a placeholder bridge (`root_folder_key[..32] XOR 0xA5`), a phase-63-era stub — not real recovery.

The web already shipped a real 'vault blob v3' model (#578): two independent random 32-byte rootReadKey/rootWriteKey, ECIES-wrapped under the user pubkey; the desktop was still on the legacy v2 single-key blob, meaning a web-created vault was literally unreadable by the desktop.
The root Ed25519 IPNS keypair is HKDF-derived deterministically and is NOT stored in the vault blob — only the two ECIES-wrapped root keys are.

Frozen cross-language KAT vectors (tests/vectors/*.json, e.g. vault-v3-blob.json) exist ahead of the Rust port and must be loaded at runtime (not hardcoded) to guarantee byte-identical behavior with the TS implementation.
cargo fmt run on a crate-root lib.rs recursively reformats the whole module tree, causing false out-of-scope diffs; executors must `git checkout --` unrelated reformatted files before committing.
Fresh worktrees lack node_modules, so the husky pre-commit hook fails on `lint-staged not found` until `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is run (or `--no-verify` is used for pure-Rust changes).

code.finding: Original research's central 'JournalOp weld' (parent_metadata: FolderMetadata field) did not actually exist in this struct — a stale/incorrect research claim that caused a wasted executor attempt before being caught.

InodeKind::{Root,Folder,File} store full read-write owner state (read_key, write_key, ipns_private_key) since the FUSE mount signs and seals, not just reads — this drove the need for the write-owner materialization API.
Legacy `root_read_key = root_folder_key[..32]`, `root_write_key = read ^ 0xA5` bridge — deleted in plan 69-24 in favor of real recovered KeyState.root_read_key/root_write_key.
v3 format: `0x03 | u16_BE(readLen) | ECIES(rootReadKey) | u16_BE(writeLen) | ECIES(rootWriteKey)`, added additively alongside the untouched v2 codec.

workflow: Persist a durable scratchpad/handoff file across pauses and session-limit deaths so multi-hour, multi-session grinds don't lose state.

Independently verify a sub-agent's architectural-blocker claims (via grep/read) before accepting them as fact or escalating to the user — agents are usually right but their evidence should be spot-checked.

Distinguish 'usage/session-limit death' (zero edits made, safe to just retry) from 'architectural blocker' (zero edits made deliberately, needs a human decision) — both return similarly but require different responses.

For a large atomic migration that can't have a compiling intermediate state, decompose into bounded 'slices' committed sequentially on one branch, each RED-tolerant except the last — this lets the grind survive session-limit interruptions without losing prior slices.

Maintain a strict 'workspace-green after every wave merge' invariant; when a plan is intentionally sdk-green/workspace-red (e.g., 69-18), hold its merge until the paired plan (69-09) restores full green, then merge as one combined unit.

When an executor unilaterally halts with 'no edits, architectural blocker,' that is the correct behavior per this repo's convention — writing speculative/unverifiable code to look complete is explicitly forbidden.

friction: gsd-planner suffered an API crash mid-plan-generation (connection closed), requiring filesystem-fallback recovery via a fresh single-plan planner.

Three successive architectural blockers were discovered only during execution (missing write-plane emit API, missing write-owner tree materialization, missing JournalOp reshape/root-key infra) despite research and plan-checker gates having passed — repeated re-scoping cost significant time.
The GSD commit helper repeatedly reported false-negative 'commit_failed' even when commits landed cleanly, requiring manual git log verification after every commit.
Executors hit account session/usage limits mid-task twice, killing agents with zero progress saved (though also zero work lost).
The Slice 5 runbook badly under-scoped the remaining work ('mechanical field-repointing') versus the actual ~250 test-compile errors and a full refresh-pipeline redesign that were needed.
cargo fmt crate-root drift repeatedly polluted diffs across many plans, requiring manual reversion of out-of-scope reformatted files in nearly every executor run.
The desktop root-key-recovery stub was not caught until after the phase was reported 'complete', forcing a late user correction and ~10 additional plans/executor runs.
open_items: Plan 69-14 (WinFsp/Windows integration, TEST-03/SC#5) is `autonomous:false` and requires the user's Windows machine — not started.
ROT-07: shared-scope-exit deletes/renames on Unix currently fail closed (EIO) because no production RotationDeps implementor is wired yet; only private deletes are fully functional.
File `versions` are not reconstructed on write after the node/v3 flip — a versioning regression flagged for verification at the desktop-e2e gate.
Replay does not unpin the old parent CID after re-publish, leaving GC-able orphaned IPFS pins (non-correctness-critical).

Plan 69-25 (fix the desktop-e2e verifier to use node/v3 SealedChildRef traversal) had not been executed by end of transcript, and the actual desktop-e2e run (the user's stated completion bar) had not yet been performed.
Recycle-bin restore (69-19) only migrated the restore *data* to node/v3 — no live FUSE restore command exists yet to consume it.
Vault export/import is not currently wired on this branch; the dead decrypt.rs helpers were deleted rather than migrated.
